Name: 84 Hours Anoxic Naturals
Desc:
Coffee cherries are hand picked at their peak ripeness to ensure high quality beans. The outer skin is removed using a depulping machine, leaving beans covered in mucilage. Unlike traditional methods, fermentation occurs in oxygen free tanks. The beans ferment in these sealed tanks for about 84 hours, which influences their flavor and aroma. After fermentation, the mucilage remains as the beans are dried on raised beds or patios under controlled conditions for even drying. 
 Located in Chikmagalur, Sai Ashirwad estate is renowned for growing various coffees, including Arabica SLN 795,CxR and Robusta Old Peridenia. The farm has organic certification, showcasing its commitment to sustainable practices. Beyond coffee, it is a haven for wildlife like Indian Gaur and Malabar Giant squirrels. The estate features its own processing unit and drying yards to ensure careful handling of beans. Additionally, water harvesting ponds reflect their focus on environmental stewardship.

Tasting_Notes: This is a 72-hour natural
Desc: This is a 72-hour natural processed coffee grown at Ratnagiri Estate at 4400 feet in the Line Patte block. The cherries, with a Brix of 25.2 at harvest, were fermented for 72 hours with a specific yeast and lactobacillus culture in stainless-steel fermenters. After fermentation, the coffee was dried slowly on raised beds over 29 days with constant stirring.

Name: Blossom Washed
Tasting_Notes: This is a 90-hour CULTURE
Desc: This is a 90-hour CULTURE PROCESS washed coffee from the Catuai varietal at our Ratnagiri farm, located at 4,300 feet in the Betamare Patte block. The cherries, with a Brix of 23.2 at harvest, were fermented in stainless-steel fermenters after removing floaters, using a specific strain of yeast and lactic acid bacteria. Following fermentation, they were depulped, washed, and slowly dried on raised beds for 26 days, enhancing their unique flavor profile.

The result is a coffee rich in flavor and exceptional quality.

Name: Excelsa community
Process: ing techniques to highlight the finest
Desc:
We hand-pick fully ripe, deep red cherries with high sugar content, ensuring minimal defects and consistent quality. After harvesting, cherries are sorted in water; ripe cherries sink while underripe or damaged ones float and are removed.  Sorted cherries are spread in thin layers on raised beds in a ventilated polyhouse, which controls temperature and protects against rain and UV exposure. We turn the cherries manually to ensure even drying and prevent fermentation. Regular raking promotes airflow, enhancing the final flavor. In the evenings, cherries are covered to shield them from moisture. We monitor moisture levels, aiming for 11–12% to preserve flavors and minimize microbial risks. After drying, cherries are packed in jute sacks and stored for at least two months to stabilize and mature. 
 The Mooleh Manay estate is situated near the scenic backwaters of the Harangi Reservoir in Coorg, Karnataka. It employs a data-oriented strategy for farming and coffee processing, as it believes that data plays a crucial role in enhancing agricultural practices and achieving top-quality coffee production. The estate grows various coffee types, such as Arabica, Robusta, and Excelsa, and utilizes careful processing techniques to highlight the finest flavors. The estate is dedicated to ongoing improvement and innovation and engages in research focused on indigenous Indian Coffea species and soil health.

Name: Kenyan Washed
Tasting_Notes: After harvesting, ripe coffee cherries are brought to the factory by smallholder
Process: ing, where the skin and pulp are removed
Desc: After harvesting, ripe coffee cherries are brought to the factory by smallholder farmers for wet processing, where the skin and pulp are removed. This process relies on electrical pumps to bring water from the nearest source into reservoir tanks. To conserve water, the factory recirculates it during processing. A disc pulper with three sets of discs is used to separate the skin and fruit from the green coffee beans. Following pulping, the coffee ferments overnight to break down sugars, then it is cleaned, soaked, and spread on raised drying tables. The drying time varies based on climate conditions and the volume of coffee being processed.

Name: Melkodige Anaerobic
Desc: Ripe red cherries with a Brix content over 24% are handpicked and washed in a water bath. They are then surface dried and inoculated with Lalcafe saccharomyces yeast. The cherries are placed in airtight containers for 72 hours of anaerobic fermentation, during which the yeast converts sugars into enzymes, esters, and alcohol, creating a unique flavor. After fermentation, the cherries are dried slowly on raised wooden trays for over twenty days.

Name: Ratnagiri AAA Washed
Desc: Ripe cherries were pulped to remove the skin and pulp while retaining the mucilage on the beans. The initial fermentation broke down the mucilage, followed by thorough washing. A second controlled fermentation ensured complete dissolution of any remaining layers, after which the parchment was left clean. The beans were then dried on raised beds under the mountain sun, allowing for gradual moisture stabilisation. This double-washed method produces a cup that is bold, clear, and refreshingly juicy.

Name: Raxidi Naturals
Desc:
After selective picking of the best coffee cherries, the cherries were washed and kept in a stainless steel container. We used a strain called W1 which is a mix of yeast and bacteria to ferment the cherries for 48 hours in an anaerobic condition. After which they were removed and taken to raised beds for slow drying for 21 days. In the drying yard a controlled environment was maintained accounting for temperature and humidity which was monitored regularly. 
 Raxidi Estate, located at an elevation of 950-1000 meters in Sakleshpur, Karnataka, spans 165 acres and has been nurtured by three generations of the Lobo family since the 1950s. Currently, father-daughter duo Richard and Rachel Lobo continue this legacy, cultivating Arabica varieties such as Selection 6, Catimore, and Chandragiri, alongside Robusta varieties like old Peredenia and Selection 270. Their focus on micro-lots and innovative processing techniques results in coffee with unique depth and character, with every step, from handpicking cherries to using pure spring water, executed with precision.

Name: RC-7 Naturals
Tasting_Notes: This is a 60-hour anaerobic fermentation natural
Desc: This is a 60-hour anaerobic fermentation natural processed coffee. It is from the Hemavathi varietal grown on our farm at 4450 feet from the block called Sivermara Patte. The Brix of the coffee cherries was 24.6 when harvested and they were put in the fermenters after floater removal. A strain of lab culture microbes were them introduced in a Nitrogen rich environment and allowed to ferment for 60 hours at 2.2 bar pressure. After removing the coffee from the fermenters, it was directly put on raised beds and dried for 29 days.

Desc: The coffee cherries which are pulped using clean spring water, effectively removing the mucilage from the seeds. To ensure consistency and uniformity in every batch, the green beans are then immersed in clean water for 24 to 30 hours. After this soaking process, the beans are dried on raised beds for 25 to 30 days. Throughout the drying process, we meticulously inspect and remove any defective beans. The remaining good beans are slow-dried until they reach an optimal moisture level of 11%.

The end product is a coffee known for its rich flavor and exceptional quality, featuring tasting notes such as sugarcane and dried coconut.

Name: The Lacto Project
Tasting_Notes: This coffee has undergone a 96-hour extended carbonic maceration
Desc: This coffee has undergone a 96-hour extended carbonic maceration. Processed naturally, made from the Hemavathi varietal, grown at 4500 feet in the SIVERMARA Patte block. The cherries had a Brix of 25.9 at harvest and were placed in Bio fermenters after floater removal. They were inoculated with various lab-grown cultures, purged with carbon dioxide, and fermented for 96 hours. After fermentation, the beans were dried slowly on raised beds for 31 days, with constant stirring.
